objectives.description: Explains that a for loop runs its body once for each item in a sequence.
Explains that range(start, stop) includes start and excludes stop.
Explains that a while loop repeats until its condition is false, so something must change it.

levels.0: Describes a loop as something unrelated to repetition.
levels.1: Says the loop repeats but believes the body runs once or runs on the whole list at once.
levels.2: Says the loop repeats code but does not connect repetitions to the items.
levels.3: Explains the body runs once per item, with the loop variable set to each item in order.

levels.0: Gives values unrelated to the range arguments.
levels.2: Gives the correct values but cannot explain the rule.
levels.3: Gives the correct values and explains that stop is excluded.

levels.0: Cannot describe what controls a while loop.
levels.1: Believes a while loop stops on its own after some time or count.
levels.2: Says the loop stops when the condition is false but not what makes it false.
levels.3: Explains the condition is rechecked each time and code in the body must eventually make it false.

misconceptions.description: Believes the loop body runs only once, or once on the whole collection.
Believes a while loop eventually stops without its condition becoming false.

questions.prompt: In your own words, what does a for loop do in Python?
hints: Think about a list of names and wanting to greet each person.

questions.prompt: For the code: for name in ['a', 'b', 'c']: print(name) — how many times does print run, and what does it print each time?
What values does i take in: for i in range(1, 5)?
hints: Try counting out loud from the first number. Where does Python stop?

questions.prompt: How many times does for i in range(3) run, and what is the last value of i?
What makes a while loop stop?
hints: Look at the line that starts with while. What is it checking?

questions.prompt: What happens if you set count = 0 and then run while count < 3: print(count), without ever changing count? Why?
